This is completely unacceptable, however the public accepts this. Firmware shouldn't even be able to be written over on non-business consumer devices without toggling a hard switch.

We could eliminate so much persistent or potential threats by adding read/write hard switches and on/off hard switches for components & sensors.

This is such a perfect solution.

This plus signed BIOS updates should be pretty much bomb-proof.

Now let's go a step further as I've thought this through, and I think you'll like this.

SD cards or USBs need to have the same hard switch feature so that their firmware cannot be overwritten without physical access. SD cards like USB devices have micro-controllers and firmware, so they need to be locked down as well. WIth that being said, let's look at what a truly secure updating process would be like:

You download the firmware update onto the SD or USB, you power down the device(since updating a device while the OS is running could allow an infected OS to do damage), toggle the write access hard-switch on, which also cuts network circuity, power on the device and it automatically takes you into firmware update where it verifies the signature of the update file, even have a hashing feature as well, for that extra verification that some might want. Once verified select to install the update. After installation, power off the device, toggle the hard-switch, viola you have just about the most secure way of hardening a device that I can think of.

In fact it's possible to make the same hard-switch system for OS and software updates, which to some of us would be a beautiful thing. It would be just about the same process and could be done in with signatures and the hashing feature.

It would mean that a virus/infection could only last until the device is restarted or powered off, no persistence.

It's a pretty damned good idea in my opinion.

One aside is that if you want to sign something, it has to be hashed anyway(as your signature is really just an encrypted hash), so that's one thing you wouldnt have to worry about.
